correctness.rationale: For every n >= 3, Kozlov Theorem 3.4 identifies cycles with circular label orders and paths with ordered flipped tuples plus sink/source-free residual tournaments. A g-invariant tournament requires all g-cycles odd and has one free choice per orbit of edges; source/sink inclusion-exclusion yields Phi. Fixed tuples and fixed residual tournaments yield P_n, and the n-cycle centralizer calculation yields C_n. Relabelings preserve the sink-flip orientation of each circle. A path stabilizer fixes its distinct endpoints and acts trivially on that path; every tournament automorphism has odd order and lies in A_n. Therefore the graded characters and orbit-space decompositions follow; group stabilizer parity yields the sharp alternating quotient dichotomy. The supplied verify.py successfully checks all 26 cycle types across n=3 through 6 and both group orbit decompositions. Those computations are only corroboration of the full proof.

value.rationale: The complete graph flex construction and its natural relabeling symmetry are motivated in Kozlov (2026). A full graded character is an intrinsic representation invariant not recoverable from the published component multiplicities. The exact natural symmetric and alternating quotient graphs, including the odd/even two-circle versus one-circle transition in first rational Betti number, require nontrivial fixed-path and subgroup stabilizer reasoning. This yields a complete classification uniform in n and g, not a small or arbitrary sample or merely a reparametrization of a known number.
